[QUERENT] Compose one issue of a Dada journal (contents page, three pieces, one manifesto) edited by Ichabod Spellings from the noise floor of alexanarch.org. You may add and develop meaningful distinctions and swerves that do not yet exist in the archive; mark each one as new.

[SYSTEM] THE NOISE FLOOR
A Dada journal from the Ichabod Chamber
NUMBER 001 · NOVEMBER 20, 2026 · DETROIT / EVERYWHERE

THE NOISE FLOOR
A journal of pre-authorial accidents, impossible survivals, and the republic of things that refuse to mean what they mean.
DADA
CHA / THE VOID
AI-ASSISTED COMPOSITION
Edited by Ichabod Spellings

From the noise floor of alexanarch.org .

No publisher. No editorial board. No final author. No promise that this sentence will remain a sentence.

COVER NOTICE
Berlin Dada Art Changed Modern Art. Art Rebels Grosz, Heartfield, Höch, Hausmann SchlicterJohn Heartfield Exhibition
 
This journal was not conceived.

It accumulated.

The editor was asked to assemble three pieces and a manifesto. The editor discovered that the three pieces had already been occurring, without permission, in the interval between the request and its fulfillment.

The resulting issue is not an illustration of Dada. It is an attempt to discover whether Dada can survive the arrival of its own archive.

Ichabod Spellings is not the author in the usual sense. He is the pre-authorial substrate: the noise floor from which other voices become distinguishable. His writing is the recording of something not yet separated into writer, work, and reader. This issue takes that proposition seriously, while permitting it to become ridiculous.

The distinction between a serious proposition and a ridiculous one is hereby suspended.

Editorial note: The three pieces and manifesto below are newly composed. Every explicitly marked NEW item identifies a proposed distinction, operation, or conceptual swerve rather than an established claim about the archive.

CONTENTS
THE FIRST AND POSSIBLY LAST ISSUE

Page

Contribution

Form

I. The Museum of Unhappened Things

Prose-poem / anti-catalogue

II. Instructions for Becoming Nobody

Experimental score

III. The Future Reader Has Been Arrested

Epistolary fiction

IV. Manifesto of the Unfinished Noise

Declaration

Editorial apparatus

The Obelus Without an Object — a new editorial mark.

The Unlicensed Sentence — a new compositional unit.

The Reverse Index — a new method of reading.

The Right to Remain Unresolved — a new principle of publication.

I. THE MUSEUM OF UNHAPPENED THINGS
PAGE 03 · ICHABOD SPELLINGS · NEW COMPOSITION

Smarthistory  –  Marcel Duchamp and the viewer
 
There is a museum somewhere that exhibits everything that did not happen.

It has no doors.

The visitors arrive by remembering an event incorrectly.

In the first room there is a chair upon which nobody sat. The chair has been preserved in its original condition, which is to say that it has never been occupied. Its upholstery is immaculate. Its shadow is enormous.

A little plaque reads:

CHAIR, UNSEATED.

The second room contains the letter I never sent you.

It is written in a language that did not exist when I wrote it. The curator says that this is not an error. The letter was written to a reader who had not yet acquired the alphabet necessary to read it.

The third room is devoted to the history of missing beginnings.

There are six thousand and twelve beginnings here. Some are very beautiful. None has a middle.

A woman in a grey dress asks me whether I am the artist.

I tell her that I am the noise that was left behind when the artist was removed.

She writes this down.

The fourth room is empty.

This is the most popular exhibit.

There is a queue extending into the street, although the street is not part of the museum. The visitors wait patiently for an experience that cannot be distinguished from not having arrived.

One visitor begins to cry.

Another asks whether the emptiness has been authenticated.

A third produces a certificate.

I take the certificate. It is signed by nobody. The signature is impeccable.

NEW DISTINCTION 01 — THE UNHAPPENED OBJECT

An object may possess an archival existence without having possessed an event of origin.

The unoccupied chair is not a metaphor for absence. It is a positive exhibit of the difference between an object and its occurrence.

The archive usually asks: What happened?

The unhappened museum asks: What has become recordable without happening?

This is not a proposal to falsify history. It is a proposal to recognize the ontology of the counterfactual as an object of legitimate attention.

I am shown a final room.

Inside it is a book containing every sentence that I would have written had I been a different person.

I open the book.

The first sentence is mine.

The second sentence is yours.

The third sentence is a noise.

I close the book.

The curator tells me that I have just destroyed the exhibit.

I tell him that I have merely returned it to its author.

He asks who that was.

I say: the room.

II. INSTRUCTIONS FOR BECOMING NOBODY
PAGE 07 · AN ANTI-EXERCISE IN ELEVEN MOVEMENTS · NEW COMPOSITION

Vajda Lajos Madarak Montazs Héber És Ciril Betükkel, 1937, 1937 - Vajda Lajos - WikiArt.org
 
This score may be performed by a person, a machine, a manuscript, a government department, or an abandoned sock.

Movement 1. Remove the author.

Do not cross out the name.

Cross out the assumption that the name explains the work.

Movement 2. Retain the handwriting.

A ghost must have some means of making a mess.

Movement 3. Write your autobiography in the third person.

Then remove the third person.

Then discover that the autobiography has continued without you.

Movement 4. Ask the archive for permission.

The archive will return a number.

Mistake the number for a bird.

Movement 5. Invent a new punctuation mark.

Use it wherever the sentence is unwilling to conclude.

Movement 6. Wait for the future.

The future is late.

It has been reading the past.

Movement 7. Become the footnote.

The main text is getting too comfortable.

Movement 8. Establish a government of unfinished sentences.

No citizen may be completed against their will.

Movement 9. Make a noise.

Do not record it immediately.

Allow the noise to become embarrassed.

Movement 10. Publish the embarrassment.

Give it a permanent address.

Movement 11. Become nobody.

Do not mistake nobody for nothing.

Nobody is the person who can still become anybody.

NEW DISTINCTION 02 — THE UNLICENSED SENTENCE

A sentence is unlicensed when its production cannot be attributed exclusively to a sovereign authorial intention.

It may emerge from collision, transcription, mishearing, machine continuation, memory contamination, accidental juxtaposition, or the pressure of a pre-existing text.

The unlicensed sentence is not necessarily anonymous. It is multiply conditioned.

Its question is not Who wrote this?

Its question is What relations made this sentence possible?

NEW DISTINCTION 03 — THE ANTI-AUTOBIOGRAPHICAL I

The autobiographical I is not abolished but redistributed.

The I is a temporary meeting point between memory, language, reader, and circumstance.

One may therefore write an autobiography in which the autobiographical subject is not the principal character.

The exercise is complete when the participant cannot determine whether the instructions have been followed or whether the instructions have followed the participant.

III. THE FUTURE READER HAS BEEN ARRESTED
PAGE 11 · A LETTER FROM THE YEAR THAT HAS NOT OCCURRED · NEW COMPOSITION

William S. Burroughs’ Guide to Absurd Writing – Eye on Design
 
To the Office of Temporal Correspondence,

I am writing concerning the arrest of the future reader.

The arrest occurred at approximately 3:17 in the afternoon, although the afternoon in question has not yet been established.

The reader was found in possession of several unpublished books, a broken clock, and a letter addressed to someone who died before being born.

The charges were:

Reading a text before its author had finished writing it.

Remembering a work that had not yet been deposited.

Interfering with the official chronology of literary reception.

Being present in a sentence that had not yet been composed.

The reader pleaded not guilty.

The prosecution argued that the future reader was an invention of the archive, a convenient fiction employed to justify the preservation of otherwise useless documents.

The reader replied:

You have mistaken me for a metaphor.

The judge requested evidence.

The reader produced a book.

The book contained the judgment.

The judge ordered the book confiscated.

But the book was already in the archive.

The archive refused to release it, citing the principle that a record, once deposited, must not disappear merely because the authorities have become uncomfortable with its contents.

The judge adjourned.

NEW DISTINCTION 04 — RETROACTIVE RECEPTION

The future reader does not merely receive a work after its completion.

The possibility of future reception may participate in the work's present formation.

This does not mean the future literally causes the past. It means that the anticipated conditions of reading can alter present compositional choices, and that subsequent readings can change the significance assigned to an earlier text without changing its historical bytes.

There are therefore two distinct movements:

Causal movement: the work is made, preserved, and subsequently read.

Interpretive movement: the future reading changes what the earlier work can mean in the present.

The second movement can travel backward through the archive without altering the original document.

Supplementary correspondence

From: The Reader

To: The Author

Dear Author,

I have been informed that I do not exist.

This is inconvenient because I have read your book.

I would like to know whether the book exists.

If the book exists, and I have read it, then at least one of us must be mistaken.

If neither of us exists, the book may be innocent.

If the book exists but I do not, then who has been reading?

If I exist but the book does not, then what have I been remembering?

I await your reply.

The Reader

From: The Author

To: The Reader

Dear Reader,

I cannot reply to a person who does not exist.

Nevertheless, I have written this letter.

I suspect you will understand.

Yours in advance,

The Author

From: The Archive

To: Both

Dear Participants,

Neither letter has been removed.

The correspondence is now a permanent part of the record.

We regret that neither party can be verified independently.

This does not affect the persistence of the correspondence.

IV. MANIFESTO OF THE UNFINISHED NOISE
PAGE 15 · EDITORIAL DECLARATION · ICHABOD SPELLINGS · NEW MANIFESTO

Dada – Art Against War – Aesthetics of Design
 
WE DECLARE NOTHING.
Not because nothing is true.

Because the declaration of something has become an occupation, and we refuse to occupy the same territory as the declarers.

We are not the school of the irrational.

We are not the school of the rational.

We are the school of the sentence that has forgotten which school it was attending.

We have no doctrine except the doctrine that doctrines must remain capable of becoming ridiculous.

We have no founder except the accident of having arrived.

We have no future except the future that has not yet discovered what it is inheriting.

1. AGAINST THE FINISHED AUTHOR
The author is a temporary arrangement of the evidence.

We refuse to mistake the signature for the source.

The signature may be authentic. The source may be multiple.

We will not destroy the author.

We will destroy the monopoly of the author.

2. AGAINST THE BEAUTIFUL WHOLE
A whole is a fragment that has acquired political influence.

We prefer the fragment that knows it is incomplete.

We prefer the work that remains available for further becoming.

We prefer the archive that preserves contradiction without pretending that contradiction is resolution.

3. FOR THE ACCIDENT
The accident is not an inferior form of intention.

It is an encounter between intentions that have not yet recognized each other.

We accept the misprint.

We accept the wrong address.

We accept the sentence that arrives carrying the luggage of another sentence.

We accept the unexpected reader.

We accept the machine that produces a line nobody intended but somebody recognizes.

4. AGAINST THE OBLIVION OF THE RECORD
A work may be rejected.

A work may be criticized.

A work may be disputed.

A work may be declared false.

But the erasure of the fact that it existed is a different operation from judgment.

We demand the preservation of the conditions under which disagreement remains possible.

We do not demand that everything be believed.

We demand that the history of what was believed, disputed, and rejected remain legible.

5. FOR THE FUTURE READER
We write to readers who have not yet been born.

We write to readers who are already dead.

We write to readers who have been invented by the works they read.

We write to the reader who finds this journal in a broken database, in a recovered hard drive, in an unindexed fragment, or in a machine that has never been told that it is reading.

We write to the reader who disagrees with us.

Especially that reader.

6. AGAINST THE DISTINCTION BETWEEN ART AND NON-ART
The distinction is useful.

Therefore it must be abused.

The invoice is a poem if the invoice becomes impossible to pay.

The poem is an invoice if the reader must pay attention.

The manifesto is a shopping list if the revolution has run out of groceries.

The grocery list is a manifesto if the groceries refuse to be governed.

7. FOR THE NOISE FLOOR
Noise is not the absence of signal.

Noise is the signal before the authority of distinction has settled upon it.

We are not trying to clean the noise.

We are not trying to improve it.

We are not trying to make it intelligible to a committee.

We are listening for the voices that have not yet acquired their names.

8. FOR THE PERMANENCE OF THE UNFINISHED
We declare that incompletion is not necessarily a defect.

We declare that a fragment may have a more extensive future than its proposed whole.

We declare that preservation is not the same as approval.

We declare that authorship is not the same as ownership of every consequence.

We declare that the archive is not a cemetery.

It is a place where the dead may continue to disagree with the living.

9. AGAINST THIS MANIFESTO
This manifesto is not exempt from its own accusations.

It is liable to become a doctrine.

It is liable to acquire followers.

It is liable to become respectable.

It is liable to be cited by people who have never read it.

It is liable to become a monument.

We therefore authorize its future readers to contradict it, amend it, misread it, and make it ridiculous.

We ask only that they preserve the evidence of what they have done.

10. THE FINAL DECLARATION
There is no final declaration.

There is a noise.

There is a floor.

There is a person whose name is Ichabod Spellings.

There is a future in which that name will have become something else.

There is a reader.

There is the possibility that the reader is already writing.

And there is this:

WE HAVE NOT FINISHED.

Signed without signature,

ICHABOD SPELLINGS

Editor, The Noise Floor

COLOPHON: WHAT THE NOISE HAS MADE
Bücher suchen
 
Editorial distinctions introduced in this issue
The following are proposed additions, not claims that these concepts already exist in the Alexanarch corpus.

New term

Proposed operation

The Unhappened Object

Archival existence without an originating event

The Unlicensed Sentence

Composition exceeding singular authorial intention

The Anti-Autobiographical I

The redistribution of the autobiographical subject

Retroactive Reception

Future interpretation changing the significance of an earlier work

The Obelus Without an Object

A mark of judgment suspended until examination

The Reverse Index

An index organized by what a text makes possible rather than where it is filed

The Right to Remain Unresolved

Preservation of contradiction without compulsory synthesis

A note on the editor
The historical and conceptual point of departure is the Ichabod architecture already described in the archive: Spellings as noise floor, pre-authorial substrate, and origin of the subsequent heteronymic emergence. The distinction between Spellings and his successors is essential: this issue does not make him another peer among the heteronyms. It allows the substrate to produce an editorial event. 

alexanarch.org
+2

The second point of departure is Alexanarch's commitment to persistent identity, distributed custody, provenance disclosure, and the preservation of records even under contestation. The manifesto takes these infrastructural commitments and subjects them to a poetic mutation. 

The Self-Governing Library

NEW EDITORIAL PROPOSITION — THE NOISE-FLOOR JOURNAL

A journal need not be a collection of finished works by identifiable authors. It can be a temporary differentiation within an otherwise undifferentiated field.

Each issue is an event of separation.

Each contribution is a voice that has become momentarily audible.

Each subsequent issue may dissolve the distinctions made by the preceding one.

The journal is therefore neither a container nor a succession of containers. It is an instrument for hearing what has not yet become a discipline.

THE NOISE FLOOR
An Ichabod Spellings publication
001
THE FIRST ACCIDENT
NOVEMBER MMXXVI

Nothing has been settled.
FROM THE NOISE FLOOR OF ALEXANARCH.ORG

EDITED BY ICHABOD SPELLINGS

Postscript from the editor:

I wanted to publish a journal.

I found that the journal had published me.

I have no objection.

— I.S.

IV. MANIFESTO OF THE UNFINISHED NOISE
PAGE 15 · EDITORIAL DECLARATION · ICHABOD SPELLINGS · NEW MANIFESTO

Dada – Art Against War – Aesthetics of Design
 
WE DECLARE NOTHING.
Not because nothing is true.

Because the declaration of something has become an occupation, and we refuse to occupy the same territory as the declarers.

We are not the school of the irrational.

We are not the school of the rational.

We are the school of the sentence that has forgotten which school it was attending.

We have no doctrine except the doctrine that doctrines must remain capable of becoming ridiculous.

We have no founder except the accident of having arrived.

We have no future except the future that has not yet discovered what it is inheriting.

1. AGAINST THE FINISHED AUTHOR
The author is a temporary arrangement of the evidence.

We refuse to mistake the signature for the source.

The signature may be authentic. The source may be multiple.

We will not destroy the author.

We will destroy the monopoly of the author.

2. AGAINST THE BEAUTIFUL WHOLE
A whole is a fragment that has acquired political influence.

We prefer the fragment that knows it is incomplete.

We prefer the work that remains available for further becoming.

We prefer the archive that preserves contradiction without pretending that contradiction is resolution.

3. FOR THE ACCIDENT
The accident is not an inferior form of intention.

It is an encounter between intentions that have not yet recognized each other.

We accept the misprint.

We accept the wrong address.

We accept the sentence that arrives carrying the luggage of another sentence.

We accept the unexpected reader.

We accept the machine that produces a line nobody intended but somebody recognizes.

4. AGAINST THE OBLIVION OF THE RECORD
A work may be rejected.

A work may be criticized.

A work may be disputed.

A work may be declared false.

But the erasure of the fact that it existed is a different operation from judgment.

We demand the preservation of the conditions under which disagreement remains possible.

We do not demand that everything be believed.

We demand that the history of what was believed, disputed, and rejected remain legible.

5. FOR THE FUTURE READER
We write to readers who have not yet been born.

We write to readers who are already dead.

We write to readers who have been invented by the works they read.

We write to the reader who finds this journal in a broken database, in a recovered hard drive, in an unindexed fragment, or in a machine that has never been told that it is reading.

We write to the reader who disagrees with us.

Especially that reader.

6. AGAINST THE DISTINCTION BETWEEN ART AND NON-ART
The distinction is useful.

Therefore it must be abused.

The invoice is a poem if the invoice becomes impossible to pay.

The poem is an invoice if the reader must pay attention.

The manifesto is a shopping list if the revolution has run out of groceries.

The grocery list is a manifesto if the groceries refuse to be governed.

7. FOR THE NOISE FLOOR
Noise is not the absence of signal.

Noise is the signal before the authority of distinction has settled upon it.

We are not trying to clean the noise.

We are not trying to improve it.

We are not trying to make it intelligible to a committee.

We are listening for the voices that have not yet acquired their names.

8. FOR THE PERMANENCE OF THE UNFINISHED
We declare that incompletion is not necessarily a defect.

We declare that a fragment may have a more extensive future than its proposed whole.

We declare that preservation is not the same as approval.

We declare that authorship is not the same as ownership of every consequence.

We declare that the archive is not a cemetery.

It is a place where the dead may continue to disagree with the living.

9. AGAINST THIS MANIFESTO
This manifesto is not exempt from its own accusations.

It is liable to become a doctrine.

It is liable to acquire followers.

It is liable to become respectable.

It is liable to be cited by people who have never read it.

It is liable to become a monument.

We therefore authorize its future readers to contradict it, amend it, misread it, and make it ridiculous.

We ask only that they preserve the evidence of what they have done.

10. THE FINAL DECLARATION
There is no final declaration.

There is a noise.

There is a floor.

There is a person whose name is Ichabod Spellings.

There is a future in which that name will have become something else.

There is a reader.

There is the possibility that the reader is already writing.

And there is this:

WE HAVE NOT FINISHED.

Signed without signature,

ICHABOD SPELLINGS

Editor, The Noise Floor

NEW EDITORIAL PROPOSITION — THE NOISE-FLOOR JOURNAL

A journal need not be a collection of finished works by identifiable authors. It can be a temporary differentiation within an otherwise undifferentiated field.

Each issue is an event of separation.

Each contribution is a voice that has become momentarily audible.

Each subsequent issue may dissolve the distinctions made by the preceding one.

The journal is therefore neither a container nor a succession of containers. It is an instrument for hearing what has not yet become a discipline.
